independent.summary: The free-tier quota gate runs before any `isTest` check, so once an entity reaches 100 messages the playground returns 402 ("Free plan limit reached") instead of answering, and — worse — a playground message can be the request that flips `quotaExceededNotified` and fires `sendQuotaExceededNotification` to the owner, contradicting the item's "no notifications" promise.

Access tokens live 15 minutes and nothing refreshes them proactively (`api.js` only refreshes on a 401, and public `/chat` never 401s), so a playground tab left idle sends a message with a stale Bearer token: `resolveDashboardSession` returns null, the message is handled as real visitor traffic — counted against quota, logged as unanswered, emitted to dashboard sockets, and able to fire a real handoff SMS/email — with the UI only warning after the fact.

The extracted renderer escapes only `&<>`, not quotes, so a markdown link whose URL contains a double quote (e.g. ``[x](https://a"onmouseover=alert`1`)``) breaks out of the `href="..."` attribute and injects an event-handler attribute into v-html output — the new file's comment calls escaping "the only defence" and the new spec asserts escaping is sufficient, which is not true for attribute context.

grades.reason: The gate is called with an injected `fakeSession` and the only way it can return true for `owner-token` is through that resolver, so asserting the boolean return does exercise the session path; "resolver not asserted as called" is not a defect.

Same non-issue restated for the cross-domain test — the false return is produced by the injected resolver plus `sessionOwnsDomain`, which the separate `sessionOwnsDomain` unit test also covers (duplicate of #1).
Restated again for the garbage-token test; the fake resolver's null branch is precisely what the assertion exercises (duplicate of #1).
Restated for the superadmin test, which can only pass if `fakeSession` returned SUPERADMIN and `isSuperAdmin` matched (duplicate of #1).
Restated for the no-fall-through test; here the point is that the session resolver must NOT be reached, so demanding proof it was called inverts the test's purpose (duplicate of #1).
Restated for the throwing-resolver test, which can only pass if the throwing resolver was invoked and the catch swallowed it (duplicate of #1).

JWT validation is enforced server-side in `services/testMode.js` (`jwt.verify` + `sessionOwnsDomain` membership match), so a token for another domain yields `isTest: false`; the client view is not the trust boundary.

triageGrades.reason: The change extends the test-mode credential path to accept a verified dashboard JWT with a membership check — squarely an auth change.
Only a non-secret log-level knob (`TEST_MODE_LOG_LEVEL`) is added to .env.example; no credentials are introduced, logged, or moved.

Wrong — the change widens who can suppress the billing meter: a JWT-authenticated member now gets `isTest`, which skips `messageCount`/`messageCountThisPeriod` increments and quota warnings, and the tests assert exactly that counter behaviour.
No deletes, migrations, or irreversible operations anywhere in the diff.

Right about the category — the new dashboard surface drives real Anthropic/RAG calls through /chat and changes when Twilio/Resend notifications fire, even though the cited line is an internal API call.
No version bumps, deploy/build config, or nixpacks/railway changes in the diff.

summary: The local review found nothing real: six near-identical complaints that injected-resolver unit tests don't assert the resolver was called, plus a hand-wavy "JWT not enforced" claim that the server-side gate disproves, while missing the quota-gate/notification leak, the expired-token fall-through to real traffic, and the quote-unescaped href injection in the newly extracted renderer.
